rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Goal: finish the ~4-5 m course in under 3 s (about 1.5 m/s or more) while staying on the 25 mm tape. Geometry: five sensors spaced 15 mm apart across x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, 0.05 m ahead of the axle, using the 12 mm footprint. That spacing covers the 25 mm tape with overlap, so at least one sensor usually reads the line even on tight bends. The track is 120 mm wide, a moderate wheelbase for stability, with a 30 mm wheel radius and 0.8 kg mass. Controller: sensor weights are proportional to sensor x ([2, 1, 0, -1, -2]), so the signal is positive (steer left) when the line is left of centre, and the signal scale is set by the weights. base_speed 1.6 (about 80% of full PWM) aims for speed without saturating the wheels in the bends. kp 3.0 gives roughly 1050 PWM counts per unit signal, a moderate correction. ki 0 avoids integral windup on the curves. kd 0.15 damps overshoot without amplifying sensor noise much. line_loss last_direction keeps the robot turning the way it was going when the line is lost at a sharp bend. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with rms_error well under 0.02 m. The main risks are overshoot on the slalom (raise kd or lower kp) and running too slowly to finish under 3 s (raise base_speed). Measurements requested below will show which of these occurs.
